experts.name: Chris DuBois
experts.title: Founder and Coach, Dynamic Agency OS
experts.headline: I help sub-$1M agencies stop depending on referrals with positioning so clear it does the selling for them.
experts.bio: Chris DuBois coaches founders of sub-$1M agencies on positioning, messaging and offers, so new work keeps coming in during their busiest delivery weeks instead of depending on referrals. His skills encode how he edits and reviews agency copy: cutting short-form copy down to one sharp claim, and reading a finished page as the real buyer to find where trust breaks.

experts.name: Gary Magnone
experts.title: Fractional Operations Leader, Highrise
experts.headline: I help agency leadership teams align on growth priorities and build the execution capacity to make them move.
experts.bio: Gary Magnone has spent 15+ years on the agency side across strategy, delivery, accounts, operations and growth, and now works as a fractional operator embedded with agency leadership teams. His skills encode how he runs the conversations that turn a vague "delivery is painful" into one quantified problem, a price the owner has already justified, and a booked next step.

experts.name: Robert Kaminski
experts.title: Co-Founder and Partner, Fletch PMM
experts.headline: I help early-stage B2B SaaS founders position and explain their product so buyers understand it in one read.
experts.bio: Robert Kaminski co-founded Fletch PMM, a product marketing practice working with early-stage B2B SaaS companies on positioning and messaging. His work focuses on the gap between what a product does and how its buyers describe the problem it solves, and on reading sales conversations as market evidence rather than as pipeline notes.

experts.name: Tanyo Gochev
experts.title: Co-Founder & Head of GTM, The Demand Department
experts.headline: I help B2B founders build outbound that books sales calls, with cold email, LinkedIn outreach and LinkedIn content run as one system.
experts.bio: Tanyo Gochev is Co-Founder and Head of GTM at The Demand Department, which builds outbound systems for B2B companies: cold email, LinkedIn outreach and LinkedIn content run together. His skills encode the parts of that work he does every week: writing outreach a busy buyer can read in one pass, using LinkedIn posts to build relationships with founders in his market, and working a revenue goal back into a weekly outreach number.

experts.name: Tony Dowling
experts.title: Director, CONVRG
experts.headline: I fix founder-led B2B sales teams with forward commercial maths, a management rhythm and the Four Pillars sales operating system.
experts.bio: Tony Dowling has spent three decades selling and running sales teams, and now leads the sales-transformation side of CONVRG, a HubSpot adoption specialist for founder-led B2B firms. He created the Four Pillars framework, which sets how a business should sell and how its managers coach and enforce that standard. His skills encode the daily and weekly mechanics of that system: the targeting angles, the 15-minute diagnostic call, the Friday reconciliation, the 80/55/35 coverage maths, and the interview that stops a manager hiring a professional interviewee.

skills.title: Activity incentive sprint
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales team's pattern needs interrupting for a few days: Call 1 bookings have dried up, presentations have stalled, a dormant list needs clearing, or the quarter needs a jolt. Produces an Executive Sprint Brief for a 1-day blitz, 3-day push or 2-week sprint, with targets worked from the team's real baseline, qualifying criteria, a scoreboard, a reward and three daily huddle prompts. Also use for "sales blitz", "sprint incentive", "spiff", "activity competition", "get the team booking meetings this week".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Buyer read
skills.description: Use this skill when a finished page, deck, or piece of client copy is about to go to the client or be published, and a real ICP or buyer research document exists. Produces a ranked list of what would make the target buyer stop trusting it, read in character, with every finding citing a line in a real source, plus what to cut and a score. Catches what craft reviews miss: scenarios that can't happen in the buyer's week, an offer never plainly stated, missing price, unused proof, seller vocabulary. Also use for "/buyer-read", "review this as the buyer", "have the ICP look at this", "what would a CFO think of this page", "be hypercritical about this copy". Not for grammar or voice checks, and never for rewriting.
skills.creator: chris-dubois

skills.title: Candidate interview coach
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales manager is about to interview a salesperson, has just finished one, or is about to make an offer. Three modes: /prep turns a CV or LinkedIn profile into red flags, forensic commercial-maths questions, a 45-second cold-call roleplay and accountability probes; /evaluate scores interview notes or a transcript on five dimensions with a hire, conditional or reject call; /contract generates a signature-ready Pre-Employment Accountability Agreement. Also use for "interview questions for a sales hire", "is this candidate any good", "sales rep CV review", "accountability agreement", "forensic interview".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Client list and stack pitch
skills.description: Use this skill when a rep's account list needs reviewing: a list meeting is due, the book is over capacity, or expansion revenue has gone quiet. Produces a prioritised table of every account with tier, days since last meaningful touch, health status (Healthy, Inactive Alert, Eviction Candidate, Flag On Track, Flag Expired) and an account-specific stack pitch angle, plus a capacity line and the week's 3 to 5 moves. Also use for "list review", "rent the list", "which accounts should Danny drop", "eviction candidates", "stack pitch", "expansion angles for my book".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Commercial KPI scoreboard
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales manager or rep asks how the numbers look for a rep or the whole team over today, this week, this month or the quarter. Produces a six-row scoreboard from live CRM deal data: presentations made, closing ratio, sales velocity, average order value, current billing, and position against target, with a 2 to 3 line commercial read. Also use for "how is Danny doing this month", "team scoreboard", "closing ratio", "sales velocity", "are we on target", "KPI check".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Commercial telemetry coach
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales manager or founder needs to install or run forward commercial discipline: setting up the five-tab telemetry workbook (/setup-telemetry), checking booked percentage, gap and 3x coverage per rep across the next three months (/check-coverage), or auditing whether the workshop outputs and workbook are present and current (/audit). Produces, by mode, a built workbook, a per-rep coverage table with this week's prescriptions on the floor, or a pass/fail checklist. Also use for "target to booked to gap to pipeline to coverage", "telemetry check", "are we covered for next month", "set up the commercial workbook".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Delivery audit discovery call
skills.description: Use this skill when you have 30 minutes with the owner of a professional service firm or agency (an existing customer, a closed-lost contact, or a net new prospect) to find the one client-delivery problem worth building a custom solution or pilot for. Produces a quantified pain (annual dollar figure plus opportunity cost in the owner's own words), a price framing delivered on the call, and a booked next step. Also use for "delivery audit", "AI audit call", "discovery call for a custom build", "scope a pilot", "find the gnarliest workflow", "price on the call".
skills.creator: gary-magnone

skills.title: Friday reality review
skills.description: Use this skill on Friday afternoon, or whenever a week's commitments need reconciling against what actually happened, per rep and for the team. Produces a Friday Wrap Scoreboard: won and lost, presentations, Call 1s held versus booked, versus target, slipping deals with the reason from call notes, a category per rep (Delivered, At Risk, Blocked) and three coaching questions for each Friday one-to-one. Also use for "Friday wrap", "what slipped this week", "Monday commitments versus Friday", "weekly reconciliation", "who is at risk this week".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: LinkedIn shoutout post
skills.description: Use this skill when you want to publicly praise a B2B founder or company for something they do well in go-to-market, and break down why it works. Produces a ready-to-paste LinkedIn post, a first comment, and a source list for every claim. Also use for "shoutout post", "shout out [name]", "celebrate this founder", "who's doing it right", "positive breakdown post".
skills.creator: tanyo-gochev

skills.title: Objection comeback coach
skills.description: Use this skill when a rep has just heard a brush-off ("send me some info", "we already have someone", "call back in six months", "no budget", "I need to run it past the board") and needs the team's own tested comeback before the next dial. Produces a cheat-sheet: the recorded comeback from the team's Comeback Book as a word-for-word spoken script, variants to choose from, a 3-line email version, and a pivot to the 15-minute diagnostic Call 1. Also use for "what do I say when they say X", "objection handling", "comeback for the incumbent objection", "they told me to email them".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Plain-language copy check
skills.description: Use this skill before any outreach or marketing copy goes out: a cold email, a LinkedIn DM, a follow-up, a post, a landing page section, a call script. Produces the copy rewritten to a 5th-grade reading level, with a pass/fail line for each check. Also use for "make this simpler", "too corporate", "plain English", "reading level", "sounds like a consultant", "would a busy founder get this". Not for sharpening a single headline or tagline.
skills.creator: tanyo-gochev

skills.title: Price defence and trade
skills.description: Use this skill the moment a rep reports price pushback on a live deal and has a call or meeting coming. Produces a one-line diagnosis of the real cause (budget, competitor, or procurement testing nerve), a value re-anchor script, a concession trading matrix of three "give X to get Y" trades drawn from the firm's own menu, and a walk-away line, plus a printable takeaway. Also use for "they want a discount", "price objection", "competitor is cheaper", "procurement is squeezing us", "how do I hold the price", "negotiation prep".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Punch-up
skills.description: Use this skill when a piece of short-form copy (headline, subhead, hero, CTA, subject line, tagline, ad line, bio, or short section) is wordy, soft, or forgettable. Produces a sharper rewrite, one or two alternates on a different angle, and a score against a six-dimension rubric, revised until it passes. Also use for "/punch-up", "make this punchier", "make this catchier", "tighten this", "this is too wordy", "cut this down", "sharpen this headline". Not for the body of a blog post or newsletter, and not for writing a page from scratch.
skills.creator: chris-dubois

skills.title: Revenue goal funnel math
skills.description: Use this skill when a founder sets a revenue or income goal and needs to know what it takes each week, or when a weekly review shows the goal slipping. Produces a backwards funnel from the goal down to weekly outreach volume, the actual-versus-required gap at every stage, and the one bottleneck to fix this week. Also use for "how many calls do I need", "reverse funnel", "goal math", "what's the bottleneck", "are we on pace", "weekly pipeline review".
skills.creator: tanyo-gochev

skills.title: Sales call market analyzer
skills.description: Analyze batches of intro, discovery, or early-stage B2B sales calls to reveal whether the prospects entering a funnel represent one coherent market or multiple distinct market segments. Use when ChatGPT needs to inspect sales-call transcripts from uploads, pasted text, or connected call-recording sources and extract each prospect's specific job-to-be-done framing, current solution or competitive alternative, persona, and company firmographics; conservatively cluster genuinely equivalent patterns; surface fragmentation and dominant segment signatures; and teach the user how to interpret the evidence without summarizing meaningful differences away.
skills.creator: rob-kaminski

skills.title: Target plan and coverage
skills.description: Use this skill when a rep or a manager needs to know whether the next three months are covered: Monday planning, a monthly review, or any "are we going to hit it" question. Produces a per-month table for Month 0, +1 and +2 with target, booked revenue, the 80/55/35 booked benchmark, the gap, qualified pipeline and the 3x coverage verdict, plus where to focus. Also use for "pipeline coverage", "target plan", "booked versus target", "gap to target", "am I on track for next month", "Monday coverage run".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Targeting strategy ideas
skills.description: Use this skill when a rep names a prospect or a sector and needs a sharper reason to call than "introduce ourselves". Produces 3 to 4 commercially provocative idea angles, each with the angle, the consequence of doing nothing, and a 2 to 3 sentence phone opener to secure a 15-minute diagnostic call, grounded only in services the firm actually sells. Also use for "give me an angle on X", "ideas for approaching the Y sector", "what do I say to get the meeting", "targeting ideas", "phone opener for a prospect".
skills.creator: tony-dowling
